name: Psycho Poker
description: Psycho Poker is a poker variant in which players wager over which hand is best according to the game's rules, with psychological or unusual rule twists typical of home-game variants. Standard poker hand rankings apply.

overview.description: Psycho Poker is a poker variant in which players wager over which hand is best according to the game's rules, with psychological or unusual rule twists typical of home-game variants. Standard poker hand rankings apply.

history.origins: Poker was popularized in the American South in the early 19th century. Psycho Poker is a home-game or dealer's-choice style variant with psychological or unusual rules, documented in poker variant sources.
timeline: 19th century: Poker popularized in American South; Psycho Poker documented as home-game variant with psychological or unusual rules.
history.cultural: Reflects American home-game culture of varying standard poker with house rules.
history.evolution: Emerged as a poker variant emphasizing psychological play or non-standard rules within the standard comparing-hand framework.

setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles; player to dealer's right cuts. Dealer deals five cards to each player one at a time, face-down, beginning with the player to the left. Remaining deck forms the stock.
setup.equipment: Standard 52-card deck and poker chips (or equivalent) for betting.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best five-card hand at showdown, or by being the last player remaining after all others fold.
rules.gameplay: After the deal, a betting round begins (player to dealer's left acts first). Players may check, bet, call, raise, or fold. Action proceeds clockwise. When the betting round ends with more than one player remaining, showdown occurs: players reveal their hands and the highest hand according to standard poker hand rankings wins the pot. Psycho Poker may add psychological or unusual rule twists per house rules.
keyRules: Standard poker hand rankings (high): straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, one pair, high card.

strategy.basic: Play tight and value strong hands; fold weak hands. Position matters: acting later allows you to see others' actions first.
strategy.intermediate: Use bluffing sparingly; balance your range so opponents cannot read you. Consider pot odds when calling or raising.
strategy.advanced: Adjust to opponents' tendencies and table dynamics; exploit predictable players. Psychological reads matter in home-game variants.
tips: In no-limit, bet sizing can force folds or extract value.
Avoid showing bluffs if you want to be paid off later.

scoring.winCondition: Highest standard poker hand at showdown wins the pot; or win by being the only player left after all others fold.
